stories.h: At least 109 migrants die in shipwreck off Djibouti
stories.w: The International Organization for Migration said the overcrowded boat carried 305 people toward Yemen when it capsized. Fifteen children were among the dead, more than 80 people survived and at least 116 remained missing.

stories.h: Riyadh airport stays closed after attack kills 12 and wounds more than 300
stories.w: Saudi Arabia kept its main airport shut and moved capital-region schools online as Yemen's Houthis threatened further strikes. The attack on domestic terminals marked a major escalation and increased risks to regional aviation, energy infrastructure and the wider US-Iran conflict.

stories.h: German ex-spymaster's arrest triggers demands for intelligence reform
stories.w: Former BND chief August Hanning is accused of obtaining nearly 2,000 internal documents through a former aide and exploiting intelligence for private clients. He denies passing secrets to foreign powers, but the case has shaken allied trust and prompted calls for tighter post-service lobbying rules.

stories.h: Hurricane Isaias leaves four dead and hundreds of thousands without power
stories.w: The storm weakened after striking the Gulf coast, but flooding and tornado risks persisted across the US southeast. Outages peaked above 850,000, and the Energy Department authorized an emergency exchange of up to four million barrels of crude oil.

stories.h: Australia rules out Russian fuel as global supply pressure grows
stories.w: Energy minister Chris Bowen said Australia would not reward Russia for its invasion of Ukraine after the US agreed to buy Russian diesel. Canberra reported 43 days of petrol and 31 days of diesel reserves, with 51 fuel ships and 3.2bn litres contracted for delivery.

stories.h: Brazil's presidential runoff puts Amazon protections at risk
stories.w: Former environment minister Marina Silva warned that frontrunner Flávio Bolsonaro could dismantle rainforest and Indigenous protections restored under President Lula. Amazon deforestation has fallen nearly 50% under Lula, but Bolsonaro led the first round by more than two million votes.
